page: Vultr voc-c-2c-4gb-50s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server instance featuring an AMD EPYC processor with an x86_64 architecture. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core, and is bundled with 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPU resources are included on this instance.

Performance benchmarks show a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng benchmarks, placing in the top 10%, and strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core CPU performance and large-block memory bandwidth fall into the average range. Passmark CPU tests, database operations, and Redis SET operations are relatively weak, placing in the bottom 25%, while static web serving throughput is poor, registering at 2.49 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable compute performance for workloads that require sustained CPU resources without the risk of noisy-neighbor interference, though the low memory-to-vCPU ratio limits its memory-intensive utility. This server is best suited for lightweight single-threaded processing tasks, basic utility services, and small-scale development environments rather than high-throughput web serving or database-heavy applications.
